svg.title: Fullmag DMI Variants: Moriya Symmetry and Stabilized Chiral Textures
svg.desc: Three-panel comparison of Fullmag's three Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction operators: (a) conventional interfacial DMI (C_nv symmetry, Néel cycloid and Néel skyrmion), (b) isotropic bulk DMI (T/O B20 symmetry, Bloch helix and Bloch skyrmion), and (c) rotated interfacial DMI stabilizing an in-plane Göbel 2019 bimeron.
svg.text: Fullmag DMI Variants: Moriya Vector Symmetry and Stabilized Chiral Textures
Three distinct operators (InterfacialDMI, BulkDMI, RotatedInterfacialDMI) — chirality is selected by sign(D) and never silently aliased
Non-centrosymmetric bulk crystal without interface normal
3D volume curl invariant; boundary law 2A ∂ν m + Db (m×ν) = 0
1D Bloch Helix (y–z plane transverse to x, Db > 0):
Spin-rotated operator stabilizing in-plane meron pairs
In-Plane Easy Axis (mbg = +x̂, Ku1 along x̂)
Spin rotation maps out-of-plane skyrmion → in-plane bimeron
2A ∂n m + D(nx mz − ny my, ny mx, −nx mx)T = 0
wrDMI = D (mz ∂x mx − mx ∂x mz + mx ∂y my − my ∂y mx)
HrDMI = (2D / μ0 Ms) (∂x mz − ∂y my, ∂y mx, −∂x mx)T
Differentiates in x,y only; integrated across full film thickness.
• Separate term: cannot mix with InterfacialDMI on same study.
• Open boundaries with D ≠ 0 require A > 0 (coupled BC).
• FEM static-periodic rDMI rejected; Göbel case uses FDM.
• Textures only set m0; dynamics decide bimeron stability.
Historical 15-check GPU run; current 19-check run NOT VERIFIED.
